analysis.detail: JDK Security component (resource resolving) vulnerability, part of Oracle's August 2026 CPU. A successful attack yields at most limited read access.

vulnerabilities.description: An integer overflow in the tt_var_load_item_variation_store function of the Freetype library in versions 2.13.2 and 2.13.3 may allow for an out of bounds read operation when parsing HVAR/VVAR/MVAR tables in OpenType variable fonts. This issue is fixed in version 2.14.2.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for Liquibase Secure 5.2.0 and later, which ship a fixed JRE. Earlier releases never open a variable font: Liquibase loads no font files of its own and the image installs only static TrueType fonts.

ratings.justification: The overflow is reached only when the JDK's FreeType parses a variable font. Liquibase never loads a font file of its own and the image's only fonts are static TrueType fonts, and 5.2.0 and later ship the fixed JRE.

advisories.title: Oracle Critical Patch Update Advisory - April 2026

analysis.detail: Oracle Java SE 2D (FreeType) issue from the April 2026 Critical Patch Update, fixed in OpenJDK 21.0.11. The flaw is an integer overflow in FreeType's tt_var_load_item_variation_store, reached only while FreeType parses the HVAR, VVAR or MVAR table of an OpenType variable font. The JDK ships its own FreeType (lib/libfreetype.so), which it uses to rasterise text: 2.13.3, in range, in the 21.0.8 to 21.0.10 JREs of Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.1.1, and the fixed 2.14.2 or later from 5.2.0. Exploitation needs the JVM to open an attacker-supplied variable font. The JDK opens either a font file passed to Font.createFont or a font that fontconfig lists from the system font directories, owned by root, or from per-user font directories that only the account running Liquibase can write. No class in the jars shipped in the 5.0.0 through 5.1.1 images calls Font.createFont. The image's only installed fonts are the DejaVu TrueType fonts under /usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu, which are static fonts with no fvar, HVAR, VVAR or MVAR table. The container entrypoint runs only the Liquibase CLI and the optional lpm helper, a statically linked Go binary.

vulnerabilities.description: CVE-2025-53057 is an Oracle Java SE Security (java.security) issue from the October 2025 Critical Patch Update, fixed in OpenJDK 21.0.9 by JDK-8360937 ("Enhance certificate handling"). The fix changes how X.509 distinguished names are parsed and rendered (sun.security.util.DerValue and sun.security.x509.AVA): before 21.0.9, BMPString values containing surrogate characters were accepted, and the RFC 2253 string forms decoded PrintableString, IA5String, T61String and BMPString values as UTF-8 regardless of their encoding. The flaw is in OpenJDK code, so every OpenJDK build (Temurin, Corretto, Zulu, Oracle) before 21.0.9 is affected. The Docker image versions were read from each published image with java -version: 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.8+9, 5.0.2 and 5.0.3 ship 21.0.9+10, and later images ship 21.0.10 or newer. The Windows installer versions were read from the install4j jreBundle setting at each release tag: 5.0.0 through 5.0.4 bundle jdk-21.0.8+9, and 5.1.0 and later bundle 21.0.10 or newer.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Upgrade to Liquibase Secure 5.1.0 or later. Docker images include the fix from 5.0.2, and Windows installers from 5.1.0 (5.0.0 through 5.0.4 installers bundle Temurin 21.0.8). When running Liquibase on your own Java (ZIP or TAR.GZ distributions), update to 21.0.9 or newer.

ratings.justification: Spoofing a server identity through this flaw needs a malformed server certificate signed by a CA Liquibase trusts. Public CAs may not issue one, and control of a trusted private CA already allows a valid certificate for the host.

advisories.title: Oracle Critical Patch Update Advisory - October 2025

analysis.detail: The Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 Docker images and the 5.0.0 through 5.0.4 Windows installers ship an affected runtime (Temurin 21.0.8); Docker images from 5.0.2 and installers from 5.1.0 ship Temurin 21.0.9 or newer and include the fix. The flawed code is present in that runtime; this assessment is that an attacker cannot exploit it through Liquibase Secure. Before 21.0.9, X500Principal.getName() in the RFC 2253 and canonical forms decoded name values as UTF-8 regardless of their ASN.1 string type, so a certificate name could render as text it does not contain. Liquibase Secure only acts as a TLS client, so the only certificate names it receives from a peer are those of the server certificates it validates. Path validation verifies every signature with the issuing CA's key, so a name can only reach any code in the process that reads it (the JDK's hostname verification, a bundled JDBC driver's own host name check, or Liquibase code) in a certificate signed by a CA the client trusts. Chain building and name constraints compare names in the affected canonical form, but a colliding issuer name only selects a candidate CA whose key must still verify the signature, and a subject that collides into a permitted subtree must still be signed by the constrained CA itself. Exploitation therefore requires a trusted CA to sign a server certificate with a deliberately malformed name. Publicly trusted CAs may not issue such certificates under the CA/Browser Forum Baseline Requirements, and an attacker able to get a trusted private CA to sign a certificate can already issue a valid one for the host, so the flaw adds nothing to that position. The JDK's own hostname verification reads SAN entries and the CN through DerValue.getAsString(), which decodes correctly. Liquibase code reads a certificate name only in DaticalTrueLicenseService, to display the holder of a license file that Liquibase signs.

vulnerabilities.description: Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: Libraries). ratings.justification: The fix only changes the String sub-range branch of AbstractStringBuilder.insert(int, CharSequence, int, int), and no code in the JRE or in the Liquibase Secure 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 images calls it with a String sub-range.

advisories.title: Oracle Critical Patch Update Advisory - October 2025

analysis.detail: Oracle Java SE Libraries (core-libs) issue, fixed in OpenJDK 21.0.9 by JDK-8359454 ("Enhance String handling"). The Java version was read from each published image with java -version: 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.8+9, 5.0.2 and later ship 21.0.9 or newer. The fix changes a single branch of java.lang.AbstractStringBuilder.insert(int, CharSequence, int, int): the one taken when the inserted sequence is a String and only part of it is inserted. A whole String now goes through the existing putStringAt(int, String) path, which copies the same bytes as the code it replaced, so the behaviour that changed is limited to inserting a sub-range of a String. A bytecode scan of the 5.0.0 and 5.0.1 images found no caller of that form. In the JRE's lib/modules, no class other than StringBuilder, StringBuffer and AbstractStringBuilder references the four-argument insert. Across all jars under /liquibase, including nested jars and the license-tracking application, its only caller is the shaded ICU class CollationIterator$SkippedState in liquibase-checks.jar, which inserts a StringBuilder, not a String. The callers of insert(int, CharSequence), which forwards the whole sequence, are in shaded ICU and the DB2 JDBC driver and insert either a StringBuilder or a whole sequence. The changed code is therefore not executed by Liquibase Secure.

vulnerabilities.description: Vulnerability in Oracle Java SE (component: JSSE) affecting Oracle Java SE 8u511, 11.0.33, 17.0.21, 21.0.13, 25.0.5 and 27.0.1 and the corresponding GraalVM releases. The private keys of eMudhra intermediate CA certificates were compromised, so an unauthenticated network attacker can present certificates the runtime accepts for any host and intercept or modify TLS traffic.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Upgrade to Liquibase Secure 6.0.1 or later. When running Liquibase on your own Java (JAVA_HOME, ZIP or TAR.GZ distributions), update to a JDK that includes JDK-8395142.
vulnerabilities.workaround: Append the 48 fingerprints listed in docker/distrust-emsign.sh to the bundled JRE's lib/security/blocked.certs (in a Windows installation, the jre folder in the installation directory), then restart Liquibase.

analysis.detail: Upgrade to Liquibase Secure 6.0.1 or later. Liquibase Secure 6.0.0 and earlier images and Windows installers bundle a Temurin 21.0.12.1 JRE that still trusts the compromised eMudhra intermediates. Builds with SECURE-1170 run docker/distrust-emsign.sh on the bundled JRE, which adds the 48 fingerprints from the upstream fix (JDK-8395142) to lib/security/blocked.certs; the JRE version string is unchanged, so scanners still report this CVE for those builds too. Until you upgrade, add the fingerprints to the bundled JRE's blocked.certs.

vulnerabilities.description: Vulnerability in Oracle Java SE (component: JSSE) affecting Oracle Java SE 8u511-b32, 11.0.33.0.2, 17.0.21.0.2, 21.0.13.0.2, 25.0.5.0.2 and 27.0.1.0.2 and the corresponding GraalVM releases. The runtime trusts eMudhra and Comodo AAA root certificates under which compromised intermediates were issued, so an unauthenticated network attacker can present certificates the runtime accepts and intercept or modify TLS traffic.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Upgrade to Liquibase Secure 6.0.1 or later. When running Liquibase on your own Java (JAVA_HOME, ZIP or TAR.GZ distributions), update to a JDK that includes JDK-8395690 and does not trust emSign Root CA - G1.
vulnerabilities.workaround: With the bundled JRE's keytool, delete every emSign and Comodo AAA entry from its cacerts (keytool -list -cacerts -storepass changeit shows them; keytool -delete -cacerts -storepass changeit -alias <alias> removes one), then restart Liquibase.

analysis.detail: Upgrade to Liquibase Secure 6.0.1 or later. Liquibase Secure 6.0.0 and earlier images and Windows installers bundle a Temurin 21.0.12.1 JRE whose cacerts still trusts the emSign roots the compromised intermediates chain to. Temurin builds cacerts from Mozilla's root store, which still trusts emSign Root CA - G1, so a Temurin update alone does not remove it. Builds with SECURE-1170 run docker/distrust-emsign.sh on the bundled JRE, which deletes every emSign and Comodo AAA root from cacerts; the JRE version string is unchanged, so scanners still report this CVE for those builds too. Until you upgrade, delete those roots from the bundled JRE's cacerts.

vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for the Liquibase Secure container. The image uses Temurin JRE and does not run as a sandboxed Java client.

ratings.justification: The assessed image is a Linux CLI container built on Temurin JRE, not an Oracle Java SE/GraalVM client runtime with sandboxed applet exposure.

analysis.detail: Oracle Java SE networking vulnerability. Liquibase Secure is built from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (core/docker/Dockerfile:1), not an Oracle Java SE or GraalVM client distribution. The container runs the Liquibase CLI through docker-entrypoint.sh rather than a sandboxed Java Web Start or applet environment (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8), so the client-only runtime required by the advisory is absent.

vulnerabilities.description: Vulnerability in Oracle Java SE and OpenJDK (component: HotSpot compiler) affecting OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later, including Java SE 17.0.21, 21.0.13, 25.0.5 and 27.0.1, 8u511-perf, and the corresponding GraalVM releases. Known as Java4Shell. On x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI, the JIT-compiled java.util.Base64 decoder miscomputes the output length for malformed padded input and writes up to 62 bytes past the end of the output array. An unauthenticated attacker who can send Base64 data to an application's decoder can corrupt the heap, leak heap memory and, with an exploit built for the application, execute code.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Upgrade to a Liquibase Secure release that bundles Temurin 21.0.13.1 or later once one is available. When running Liquibase on your own Java (ZIP or TAR distributions, or the Liquibase libraries embedded in an application), update to a JDK that includes the November 17, 2026 OpenJDK security fixes (17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1, 27.0.1.1 or later).
vulnerabilities.workaround: Start Liquibase with -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics, which turns off the vulnerable hardware-accelerated Base64 decoder. Set JAVA_OPTS to -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics before running the liquibase or liquibase.bat launcher, or pass -e JAVA_OPTS=-XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics to docker run. For an application that embeds Liquibase, add the flag to that application's JVM options.

advisories.title: Oracle Critical Security Patch Update Advisory, November 2026

analysis.detail: Liquibase Secure images and Windows installers bundle a Temurin 21 JRE (21.0.13 or earlier) that contains the vulnerable Base64 decoder. No Temurin release with the fix is available yet. Practical exposure is low for inbound attacks. Liquibase is a short-lived command-line process that accepts no inbound connections, and the Base64 data it decodes (license files, changelogs, loadData values) comes from the user. The published server exploits need many crafted requests to one long-running JVM, to warm up the decoder and arrange the heap. The remaining path is outbound: the researchers report a client-side exploit against a Java program that opens a TLS connection to a malicious server, so a run that connects to a database or service an attacker controls or impersonates may be exposed. Applications that embed the Liquibase libraries run on their own Java runtime and are affected through that runtime. Only x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI (Intel Ice Lake and newer Xeon, AMD Zen 4 and newer) are affected; ARM64 is not.

Liquibase Secure is a command-line tool that never passes image, font or other rendering data to the Java 2D APIs, so the vulnerable component is not reachable.

analysis.detail: Oracle Java SE 2D issue (the graphics, imaging and font rendering subsystem). Every published Liquibase Secure image from 5.0.0 to 6.0.0 ships a Temurin 21 JRE between 21.0.8 and 21.0.12.1, which is in Oracle's affected range, so the version alone does not rule it out. Images from 6.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.13, which contains the fix. Liquibase Secure is a command-line tool that does not render images or fonts or decode untrusted image data. Liquibase's own code references only java.awt.Desktop, which hands a generated report to the local browser after an interactive run and is skipped when Liquibase's headless setting is on. That call passes a file path to the operating system and does no 2D rendering. A scan of the bundled jars for java.awt and javax.imageio references found these other users, none of which Liquibase passes image or font data to: browser-based sign-in helpers in the cloud and JDBC drivers (Desktop only), the H2 and HSQLDB GUI tools, geometry conversion helpers in the Databricks driver and Apache Commons Math, JAXB's image binding (Liquibase's JAXB models have no image fields), and the bundled data redaction library's PDF/image path, which uses ImageIO and Java 2D but is never run because Liquibase Secure calls that library only with plain text.

analysis.detail: Oracle Java SE JDBC issue from the October 2026 Critical Patch Update. Liquibase Secure images 5.0.0 to 6.0.0 ship Temurin 21 JREs from 21.0.8 to 21.0.12.1, all in Oracle's affected range; images from 6.0.1 ship Temurin 21.0.13, which contains the fix. The only JDBC-area change in OpenJDK 21.0.13 is JDK-8383301 (Enhance WebRowSets), which hardens the XML reader and entity resolver behind javax.sql.rowset.WebRowSet. analysis.detail: Oracle Java SE JAAS issue from the October 2026 Critical Patch Update. analysis.detail: Oracle Java SE Lightweight HTTP Server (com.sun.net.httpserver) issue from the October 2026 Critical Patch Update; Oracle lists 21.0.12.1 as the last affected Java 21 release. The published Liquibase Secure images ship Temurin JRE 21.0.9 (5.0.2, 5.0.3), 21.0.10 (5.1.0, 5.1.1), 21.0.11 (5.2.0, 5.2.1), 21.0.12 (5.2.2) and 21.0.12.1 (6.0.0), so every one of them carries the vulnerable version. analysis.detail: JDK Networking (HTTP Connections) vulnerability, part of Oracle's August 2026 CPU. Liquibase Secure is built from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (docker/Dockerfile:2) and never listens on a socket; it is only an outbound network client (HTTPS to license/hub endpoints, TLS JDBC to target databases).
